transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I really hope I'm not wasting your time with this. It's probably just a bit of stress—I teach secondary school, so it gets quite busy—but... well, I came in because I've been having this issue at work. It's actually a little embarrassing to admit. 

I just... I can’t seem to shake this feeling that certain staff emails, and even the morning announcements over the PA system, are... well, that they're really coded messages about me. I know how that sounds, I really do. My colleagues are very sweet, and they’ve gently shown me that those emails were just standard messages sent to everyone on staff. And logically I know they're right, but... I still just can't stop feeling like they are directed at me. 

Does that make sense? I'm sorry, I know it probably sounds very foolish.
About how long have you been experiencing this feeling that the messages are directed at you?

Well, I suppose the worries about the emails and the announcements have been going on for... maybe about four months now? I kept hoping it would just blow over, you know, once the school term settled down. I hope I haven't waited too long to come in. 

And, um... oh dear. I should probably mention this too, because I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information, but... it's terribly embarrassing. Around that same time, so for about four months as well, there's also been... well, a voice. Just occasionally! And I sometimes find myself answering it. It's nothing bad, I promise, and I'm still doing my job perfectly fine. I just... I really hope that doesn't make me sound completely crazy to you. Is that... does that happen sometimes when people get overly stressed?
Over these past few months, how has your overall mood been feeling?

Oh, my mood? It's... it's been perfectly fine, really. Thank you for asking. 

I mean, apart from the usual tiredness you get from teaching teenagers all day, I’ve felt quite normal. I try very hard to keep a positive attitude, especially for the students. I haven't been feeling sad or down, or... or anything like that, if that's what you're checking for. I've actually been quite cheerful, mostly! Just a little flustered by those other things I mentioned, but I always make sure to keep a smile on at work. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your questions properly. I just want to be as helpful as I can.
Could you tell me a little more about that voice—what does it say to you?

Oh, the voice. Right. Well... please don't be alarmed, it's really nothing terrible, I promise. 

It mostly just happens when things are very still and quiet, you know? Like when I'm alone in my house, or... or just after the classroom empties out at the end of the school day. It's a woman's voice, and she doesn't say anything mean or frightening. Usually, she might just say my name, or make a very short little comment about whatever I happen to be doing at that exact moment. 

It sounds so clear and... and ordinary, I suppose, that I actually catch myself answering her out loud before I even realize there's no one else in the room with me. It's a bit silly of me, isn't it? I just instinctively reply out of politeness before my brain catches up. 

I really hope that doesn't sound too strange or worrying to you. It's just a very mild thing, really. Am I explaining it clearly enough? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right sort of details.
